title: Financial-condition paths do not synchronize health and unpaid-care transitions
source_unit: recontacted SHED adult respondent, paired 2024 and 2025 waves

denominator.unit: paired respondents with valid health path

observations.method: Weighted descriptive transition table from the SHED 2024-2025 paired panel; percentages are within the financial-condition path and valid health-path denominator.
observations.uncertainty: No design-based standard errors estimated; panel recontact, self-report, and broad ordinal categories introduce uncertainty.
observations.counterinterpretation: Most respondents in the worsened financial path reported unchanged or improved health; health, money, care, and time may move on different schedules.

denominator.unit: paired respondents with valid health path

observations.method: Weighted descriptive transition table from the SHED 2024-2025 paired panel; percentages are within the financial-condition path and valid health-path denominator.
observations.uncertainty: No design-based standard errors estimated; panel recontact, self-report, and broad ordinal categories introduce uncertainty.
observations.counterinterpretation: The stable financial path also contains health worsening and improvement, so financial stability is not a complete health explanation.

denominator.unit: paired respondents with valid health path

observations.method: Weighted descriptive transition table from the SHED 2024-2025 paired panel; percentages are within the financial-condition path and valid health-path denominator.
observations.uncertainty: No design-based standard errors estimated; panel recontact, self-report, and broad ordinal categories introduce uncertainty.
observations.counterinterpretation: Financial improvement did not automatically produce health improvement; 85.3% reported unchanged or worsened health in this valid path subset.

observations.period: 2024->2025; financial condition worsened; adult-care entry universe

denominator.unit: paired respondents reporting no unpaid adult care in 2024 with valid 2025 care status

adult_care_entry.unit: percent entering reported unpaid adult care

observations.method: Weighted descriptive care transition table from the SHED 2024-2025 paired panel; entry is conditional on no reported unpaid adult care in 2024.
observations.uncertainty: No design-based standard errors estimated; the measure does not observe care hours, intensity, recipient outcome, or trigger.
observations.counterinterpretation: The entry difference is descriptive and may reflect health, family composition, or other events rather than financial change itself.

observations.period: 2024->2025; financial condition unchanged; adult-care entry universe

denominator.unit: paired respondents reporting no unpaid adult care in 2024 with valid 2025 care status

adult_care_entry.unit: percent entering reported unpaid adult care

observations.method: Weighted descriptive care transition table from the SHED 2024-2025 paired panel; entry is conditional on no reported unpaid adult care in 2024.
observations.uncertainty: No design-based standard errors estimated; the measure does not observe care hours, intensity, recipient outcome, or trigger.
observations.counterinterpretation: Care responsibility can enter without a worsening financial path, so financial change is not a sufficient explanation for care transitions.

observations.period: 2024->2025; financial condition improved; adult-care entry universe

denominator.unit: paired respondents reporting no unpaid adult care in 2024 with valid 2025 care status

adult_care_entry.unit: percent entering reported unpaid adult care

observations.method: Weighted descriptive care transition table from the SHED 2024-2025 paired panel; entry is conditional on no reported unpaid adult care in 2024.
observations.uncertainty: No design-based standard errors estimated; the measure does not observe care hours, intensity, recipient outcome, or trigger.
observations.counterinterpretation: Financial improvement coexists with care entry for some respondents, which keeps the material-to-care arrow descriptive and open.

boundary: This is a weighted descriptive same-respondent panel comparison. It is not a causal estimate, detailed time-use measure, care-intensity measure, verified financial shock, trust or political-action measure, or institutional-remedy result. The retrieval hash covers the committed analysis memo because the raw public-use files and reproduction JSON are not committed.
